text: What if I told you lah yoh roh nah's legend is far older than the story of a mother drowning her children?

text: Centuries ago, the people of ancient Mexico told of a mysterious woman crying through the darkness.

text: Before the Spanish conquest, an omen described a woman wandering the streets, desperately crying out for her children.

text: Some researchers connect those cries to See-wah-koh-wat, an ancient Aztec goddess associated with motherhood.

text: Over time, another story emerged. A woman named Mah-ree-ah, betrayed by the man she loved, drowned her own children in a river.

text: Consumed by guilt and sorrow, her spirit was said to wander the rivers forever, screaming, Eye, mees ee-hos!

text: But historians have never confirmed that this tragedy happened. Different regions tell completely different versions of her story.
